text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- GOVT HUNTS DOWN CRIME MONEY AROUND THE WORLD
Brazil is due to sign accords with its Mercosur partner countries as well as with the United States to help facilitate the repatriation of funds obtained illegally in Brazil and channeled abroad.
-- HSBC LOOKING FOR A SUPER-EXECUTIVE
HSBC, the new owners of private Brazilian bank Bamerindus, are looking for a new Brazilian chief executive to run the day-to-day business of Bamerindus.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- SAO PAULO COMMITTED NO CRIME SAYS MALUF

Former Sao Paulo mayor Paulo Maluf said there were no irregularities regarding the emmission of state and municipal bonds in Sao Paulo, and he defended his successor Celso Pitta who has come under suspicion of being involved in a million dollar scandal involving such bonds.
-- MAN KILLS EX-FIANCEE AND COMMITS SUICIDE
A 23-year-old man shot dead his ex-fiancee in a Sao Paulo shopping center and then committed suicide because the woman refused to return to him.
-- BAMERINDUS OPENS TODAY AND ANNOUNCES EXPANSION
Private Brazilian bank Bamerindus opens its doors to the public today under new ownership and plans to expand the number of offices around the country.
O GLOBO
-- POLICE CLOSES GAY MINORS BAR IN MANAUS
Police closed down a bar in Manaus known to be the center for homosexual prostitution of minors.
-- CENBANK BROKE BAMERINDUS SAYS ANDRADE VIEIRA

The former owner of private Brazilian bank Bamerindus, Senator Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira accused the Central Bank of causing Bamerindus' downfall by leeking incorrect information about the bank to the press.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
